hooks.text: Jean de Valette fired the heads of prisoners from his cannons.
40,000 Ottoman soldiers arrived to conquer one tiny island.
The Knights of Malta poisoned their own wells to survive.

title: How the Knights of Malta Defied an EMPIRE 🛡️
description: In 1565, a tiny force of knights held off 40,000 Ottoman soldiers in one of history's most brutal sieges. Discover how Jean de Valette survived impossible odds.

beats.text: Jean de Valette fired the heads of prisoners from his cannons.
beats.visual: Portrait of Jean de Valette, Grand Master of the Knights of Malta, 16th century

beats.text: In 1565, between twenty-three and forty-eight thousand Ottoman invaders arrived to conquer Malta.
beats.visual: Map of the Great Siege of Malta from 1565

beats.text: To prepare, the Grand Master poisoned his own wells.
beats.visual: Engraving of knights preparing fortifications on Malta, 1565

beats.text: After Fort Saint Elmo fell, Ottomans floated decapitated knights across the harbor.
beats.visual: Painting of the fall of Fort Saint Elmo by Mattia Perez d'Aleccio

beats.text: Valette retaliated by firing his prisoners' heads back.
beats.visual: Engraving of the Great Siege of Malta showing cannon fire, 1565
queries: Great Siege of Malta cannons engraving

beats.text: The garrison held until relief arrived in September.
beats.visual: Painting of the relief fleet arriving at Malta in 1565

beats.text: But the brutal siege began when the enemy armada arrived.
beats.visual: Painting of the Ottoman armada approaching Malta, 1565
